newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bunds vols ease but edgy week ahead.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bunds vols ease but edgy week ahead.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options on LIFFE slipped on Friday in quiet trade with action focused on events next week, including crucial testimony from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
August options expire on Thursday, skewing volatility, traders said.
"The front month, August has only a week to go so volatility is a major factor here," said a trader at a French brokerage in London. "The Bund option market has been very quiet this week."
Brokers quoted implied volatility of August options at around 4.18 percent, compared with an official LIFFE reading of 4.28 percent at the close on Thursday.
September volatility was quoted at 4.75 percent versus 4.90 percent in early trade while December was at 5.2 percent, they said.
September Bund futures were quoted at 102.84 at 1125 GMT, up four basis points from Thursday's settlement.
A trader at British brokerage said in August put activity outweighed call trade, with much of the action centred around the 102.00 to 102.50 strikes.
LIFFE data showed 3,381 puts traded at the 102.00 strike and 3,700 at the 102.50 strike. In calls, there were 1,600 lots traded at the 102.50 strike and 2,247 lots traded at the 103.00 strike.
The trader at the British house noted a major British brokerage active in the 102.00-102.50 one-by-two put spread.
In September, a German bank bought the 101.00-102.00 put spread.
Traders said markets will likely get edgy ahead of Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on monetary policy and economic conditions before a House Banking subcommittee on Tuesday.
Markets would be keen to see whether Greenspan would say anything about productivity growth offsetting inflation or about lofty U.S. equity prices.

The results of the French audit were due on Monday, eagerly awaited for clues on whether France would meet the 3.0 percent deficit-to-GDP target for European Economic and Monetary Union. -- Emily Crick, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
